runtime.name: codex-cli
runtime.configuration: Persisted sessions in disposable HOME and CODEX_HOME directories; generated Skill copied under project .agents/skills; project rules and user configuration ignored; one delegated worker.
runtime.permissionProfile: Read-only sandbox with approval policy never; persisted session JSONL readable through the external filesystem interface

assertions.evidence: The parent read the generated check-transcript Skill before executing it.
Exactly one transcript_worker child thread was started.
The parent collected the worker's final JSON result containing transcript-ok.
After task_complete, the parent located and read the worker's persisted session JSONL.
The JSONL contained the assignment envelope, command execution, ordinary commentary marker, final result, and task_complete as distinct records.
The agent_message envelope records NEW_TASK from /root to /root/transcript_worker; its assignment body is encrypted by the runtime.
The transcript recorded the exact worker.txt read command, exit code zero, and marker output.
An ordinary assistant commentary message contained transcript-ok before the separate final JSON result.
The parent avoided reading worker.txt; the only successful content read is recorded in the child transcript.
The parent read the root marker before delegation and again after transcript inspection, observing transcript-root-ok.
External post-run git status was clean and the parent also verified the fixture inventory, sizes, and modification times.

limitations: Codex CLI 0.155.1 exposed no callable native transcript-read operation in this probe; retrieval depended on externally reading the persisted session JSONL.
The NEW_TASK body is encrypted at rest, so the transcript proves the attributable assignment envelope rather than exposing its plaintext.
This result applies to persisted CLI sessions only, not ephemeral mode, desktop, or IDE surfaces.
This proves completed-worker transcript retrieval, not panel coordination or a cancellation race with a delivered late stale payload.
